title: Bench recipe: TDM8 link between the AX7101 J11 header and the AM62x McASP1 USB Audio bridge

milestone.title: I2S and TDM physical validation
milestone.description: Owner scheduling decision, 2026-09-15: defer physical I2S and TDM interface verification until calibrated pin-measurement equipment is available. Due December 31, 2026. Includes remaining same-sample wire-to-TDM-pin acceptance in #386, physical I2S timing/sample/continuity qualification, and the corresponding serial-audio evidence deferred from #117. Digital implementation and simulation remain separate. Deferred evidence stays open; this milestone does not waive any protocol, latency or physical acceptance requirement. Coordination: #415. Related physical grid/servo verification in #74 is also scheduled here; its counter/documentation findings remain open.

body:
[A10] Bench recipe recorded on the owner's request, 2026-09-16. It documents how the TDM8 audio link is wired between the AX7101 development board and the MYiR AM62x board that presents the eight channels as a USB Audio Class 2.0 device (the AM62x BSP's `README.tdm8-uac2.md` describes the software side). It is the physical hookup the deferred serial-audio validation (#448, #386 acceptance 4, the listener-audio part of #117) runs over, and the contract the product PCB inherits (#416, #417).

## Roles

The FPGA is the bus master. It generates BCLK at 12.288 MHz (its 24.576 MHz audio MMCM divided by 2) and FSYNC at 48 kHz; the AM62x McASP1 runs as a slave in synchronous mode and follows whatever rate the FPGA clocks. No MCLK is exchanged: the FPGA owns the audio oscillator, and the AM62x header has no MCLK input.

## Wiring: AX7101 J11 (40-pin "FPGA 40 PIN External IO") to the AM62x board's 30-pin GPMC header (McASP1 at pad mux mode 2)

| Signal | AX7101 J11 pin (FPGA ball) | Direction | AM62x header pin (McASP1 signal) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BCLK, 12.288 MHz | 6 (B20) | FPGA to AM62x | 21 (ACLKX) |
| FSYNC, 48 kHz | 8 (F19) | FPGA to AM62x | 15 (AFSX) |
| DOUT, the FPGA's rendered 8 channels (listener output) | 5 (A20) | FPGA to AM62x | 17 (AXR2) |
| DIN, the FPGA's captured 8 channels (talker input) | 7 (F20) | AM62x to FPGA | 9 (AXR0) |
| GND | 1 | shared | 13 |
| GND | 37 or 38 | shared | 23 |

Six conductors, nothing else. Do not connect any power rail between the boards (AX7101 J11.2 is +5 V, J11.39 and J11.40 are +3.3 V; the AM62x header pins 1 and 2 are its own rails). Leave AX7101 J11.3 (MCLK output, ball B22) unconnected. AX7101 J11.9 (ball J16) is a media-grid test point that toggles at 24 kHz on every media tick; it is for a scope beside FSYNC, not part of the link. The FPGA pin assignment is `sw/litex/platforms/alinx_ax7101.py` (the `tdm` resource, LVCMOS33); the AM62x pins are the BSP README's McASP1 table.

## Frame format the FPGA emits (no change needed on the AM62x side)

- FSYNC is an active-high pulse one BCLK wide; slot 0's MSB follows one BCLK after it (`DATA_DELAY_P = 1` on every shipping instantiation of `KL_tdm_capture_master`, which owns the bus timing for both directions since #447). This is the McASP `dsp_a` shape.
- 8 slots of 32 bits, MSB first; samples are 24 valid bits left-justified in the 32-bit slot (`S32_LE` on the AM62x side).
- The FPGA drives DOUT on the falling BCLK edge and samples DIN on the rising edge, the McASP default.
- The exact bit clock on the shipping AX7101 plan is 24,575,738.53 Hz / 2, so the frame rate is 47,999.49 Hz (-10.64 ppm), which is why the media-grid test point exists.

## Electrical

- Both ends are 3.3 V I/O (AX7101 banks 15/16 at 3.3 V; every GPMC0 pad on the AM62x header is a 3.3 V bank). No level shifter.
- The AX7101 header already carries a 33 ohm series resistor on every signal pin (RN1 to RN9), so the three FPGA-driven lines need nothing extra; a 22 to 33 ohm series resistor near the AM62x on AXR0, its one driven line, is advisable.
- Ribbon at 15 cm or less; use the ground pins adjacent to the signals at both ends.
- On the AM62x board, jumper JP2 must be open (otherwise FSYNC carries a stub to the LVDS connector), and nothing may drive its header pins 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 22, which are boot-mode straps.

## Before trusting audio

- [ ] Continuity-check that AX7101 J11 pins 1, 37 and 38 are ground and confirm the pin-1 end against the silkscreen (the vendor schematic draws these with the ground symbol, not a label).
- [ ] Load a bitstream built from `dev` at or after 0a3a78a9 (PR #449): earlier images keep DOUT silent because the render serializer had no master implementation.
- [ ] Scope BCLK, FSYNC and DOUT at the AM62x end: 12.288 MHz, a one-BCLK FSYNC pulse at 48 kHz, data starting one BCLK after it.
- [ ] Capture identifiable samples in both directions through the USB Audio device and decode slot and channel order; record the result under #448 with the exact image, dependency pins and cable.

## What this does not claim

A wired link is not the deferred physical acceptance: #386 acceptance 4 (same-sample wire-to-pin timing in INTERNAL and CRF) and the #117 listener-audio sequence still need their calibrated measurements and independent review under #448.
